It's just a theory of mine. I think these rules are mostly targeting spammers and brigaders, but there's side-effects and other reasons Voat is how it is:

So subs here can set a minimum in-sub CCP to downvoat. The idea in this is that people who are not part of a community should not decide what's not seen there or be able to brigade. 1: The sitewide voating limits essentially do that for the whole site. This also helps keep the other site's cancer from spreading to here.
2: in order to voat how they want, people have to be nice to get upvoats (line up with the old guard); internet points actually sorta mean something now.
3: people who would not normally comment are commenting, drowning out the jerks, because they need CCP (see /v/lurkaholics) .
4: the site is small enough, and difficult enough to get into, that we're not yet invaded, much less controlled by certain groups with socio/politic views.
5: the site is just plain small. Reddit's community was pretty good back in the day. It took 4-5 years before the defaults turned into reposts-ville and 4-chan lite. It took a couple years after that (and a Digg implosion) for reddiquette to go out the window (votes=agreement). And it took a year after that to turn into an echo chamber.
